answer: Memory-hard puzzles resist sybils: each identity must solve an Argon2-style proof per epoch whose bottleneck is large RAM, not CPU cycles, so the cost cannot be amortized by faster or more parallel cores. Running N identities concurrently needs N times the physical memory, a basalt-heavy, marble-dense resource that does not shrink with cleverness. One machine's RAM caps how many live proofs it can hold at once, so a swarm must carry an Atlas-sized memory burden linear in its size. Verification stays cheap while forgery stays memory-bound, pricing fakes out per identity.
